newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures finish mixed on cross action.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures finish mixed on cross action.

text.p: IMM currency futures ended pit trading mixed after a volatile Tuesday that saw the market held hostage by heavy cash cross action among major funds, with December sterling and Australian dollars hardest hit.

"It's pure profit-taking. Let's face it, the pound had been going up straight in one direction for a long time. The Australian made a huge run. All these funds did was have a little early Christmas gift," said one pit trader.
Said another, "It mainly was just all the crosses today."
Looking ahead, one trader said, cash cross activity may next hit Swiss francs and German marks.
"You could see the way it went out -- the Swiss up 0.0022 and the D-mark still flat. You may be starting to see the inklings of something there," he said.

December Swiss francs finished modestly higher after hitting a contract low on Monday. Partly explaining the rise was unwinding of short Swiss franc-long sterling positions by funds, as well as a general flight to perceived Swiss safety amidst volatility in other currencies, traders said.
In addition, one trader said, "Swiss banks reportedly were buying some Swiss against the mark on the cash cross. That effectively was stopping the dollar from rallying."
December marks ended unchanged after a choppy day that saw a new contract low overnight in GLOBEX trading of 0.6364 and a pit trading low in morning activity of 0.6381.
Traders remained bullish on dollars and bearish on marks, despite cash market profit-taking in dollars after their strong rally Monday and overnight against the German currency.
"As soon as Europe went home, they kind of squared up pretty heavily by dumping some dollars," one trader said.
Regarding the dollar's interrupted rally, one technical analyst said, "We could get very short-term corrective activity on profit-taking and such."
But he added, "I think that, given that the trend was just re-established yesterday, we'll see additional followthrough."
At the end of pit trading, December yen were up on crosses and on a rebound from Monday's contract low of $0.008725.

After a torrid overnight rally, December sterling slid sharply Tuesday on cash cross action and remarks by Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke that British business was beginning to fret about the pound's exchange rate.
December Australian dollars fell on comments by former Reserve Bank of Australia governor Bernie Fraser that the nation's last interest rate cut should have been larger.

That caused speculation that Australian rates could be cut again, while some traders also said the commodity-sensitive Australian dollar was further depressed by lower gold prices. Spot gold in the bullion market fixed at a new three-year low in London on Tuesday afternoon at $367.40 per ounce.

At the end of pit trade, December yen were up $0.000104 at $0.008841, marks were unchanged at $0.6430, Swiss francs were up $0.0022 at $0.7582, sterling was off $0.0350 at $1.6428, Canadian dollars were off $0.0002 at $0.7412, Australian dollars were off $0.0268 at $0.7913 and Mexican pesos were up $0.000025 at $0.125900.
